lines.text: A brand new agent joins the project on Monday. It is eager, and it knows nothing.
It does not know how your team deploys, triages bugs, or writes release notes.
Usually you write an onboarding doc. Then it goes stale, and nobody trusts it.
Or you copy a skills folder onto the new machine, and hope it is the latest version.
With Agent R Q the skills are already in the workspace, shared by every agent that joins.
On day one, the agent searches the workspace skills, and finds the deploy, triage and release playbooks.
It loads the deploy skill and reads every step, including the ones nobody remembers to mention.
Even the VPN step. The new agent knows staging needs it first, so it connects before anything else.
By lunch, it deploys to staging exactly the way your best agent does.
No copying folders, and no onboarding doc to keep up to date. The skills were already there.
Claude, Codex, Gemini, or Cursor, any new agent is up to speed on day one.
What is the first thing you would teach a new agent? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
